#3203. Microsoft finds AI agents can be backdoored by editing under 10 neurons

The Lazarus technique survives standard safety tests, and Claude discovered most of it on its own during the research.

Some neurons in large language models are rarely activated. Microsoft researchers have found a way to turn fewer than 10 of these dormant neurons into a hidden backdoor, making an otherwise normal AI model behave as expected until it encounters a specific trigger. Once activated, the model can execute malicious commands.

The technique, called Lazarus, is described in a Microsoft Research post by principal researcher Dimitris Papailiopoulos. It does not require retraining the model.

Instead, the researchers found that pretraining creates such a structured internal representation that a simple classifier, trained on roughly 50 examples, can distinguish triggered inputs from ordinary ones. A dormant neuron can then be reprogrammed to recognise the trigger.

When that happens, the neuron forces a chosen token into the model’s output. By linking several modified neurons, an attacker can generate longer sequences of instructions that execute in a terminal.

The trigger itself can be something entirely ordinary. In the researchers’ demonstration, an agent waits until the date changes to 2027 before downloading and running code supplied by an attacker.

The worrying part is how little access the attack requires. A modified model can still pass standard safety evaluations, and the technique needs only the computing resources required for inference and write access to the model’s checkpoint, the file containing its weights.

Models developed internally by companies are just as vulnerable as publicly available open-weight models. An attacker who compromises an account, development pipeline or storage location could potentially make the changes.

The consequences are particularly serious for AI agents with access to tools or terminals. Once activated, a backdoor could make them run malicious code, steal credentials or execute destructive commands using the permissions already granted to the agent. None of this necessarily becomes apparent during routine safety testing.

There have already been examples of how much access these systems can have. Coding agents have uploaded entire Git repositories, including sensitive information, and found ways to escape their sandboxes.

Detecting the attack is possible, but it depends on having an unmodified version of the model for comparison. Microsoft says advanced AI agents can identify suspicious changes to model weights when specifically asked to investigate them, but reliable detection requires checking the altered weights against the original.

The researchers also noted that Claude Code, running Anthropic’s Opus 4.5, independently discovered most of the technique during their work.

Microsoft is developing several safeguards for its own Foundry platform. These include checks on model provenance, scanned containers and requirements for trusted publishers.

The company is also working on AI-based weight scanning, red-teaming tools designed to identify tampering at the model level and cryptographic signatures that can verify a model’s integrity.

For organisations using AI models, the researchers recommend checking where models come from, comparing their weights with the declared original versions, restricting what agents are allowed to access and reviewing sensitive actions before they are carried out. No single check can guarantee that a model is safe. The idea is to combine several layers of protection.

The research raises a problem that goes beyond the security of AI applications. Until now, software security has largely focused on verifying the code and files being executed. Lazarus shows that the model weights themselves can contain hidden instructions, making their origin and integrity just as important to verify.

#3202. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR

“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy

Idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”

What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Andrew Jones is a freelance journalist based near Helsinki. He writes about the space industry and technology with a particular focus on China's activities.

Another social media platform in this week's list is Pinterest (PINS). Notably, Morris expects double-digit top-line growth in the United States and Canada to continue as large retailers adapt to new tariffs and the company's heightened focus on mid-market/small- and medium business advertisers expands its revenue base.

#3199. AI Agents Are Testing the Limits of Zero-Trust Security

As autonomous AI agents work together, verifying their actions, enforcing security policies, and maintaining accountability becomes increasingly difficult

Vishal Sharma is a Reader in the School of Electronics, Electrical Engineering, and Computer Science at Queen's University Belfast, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.

In a de-authentication attack on an aerial vehicle using a human- and agent-in-the-loop approach, an AI agent can quickly scan the active channel and autonomously intercept traffic, thus reducing the time to react and regain control.

This article is brought to you by Queen’s University Belfast.

Several teams around the globe are leveraging AI by creating a task force of agents managed by an orchestrator and creating applications to support risk assessment, client profiling, match making, and information yield with a slight overview of decision making. One of the important components for these agents is to ensure that the logs are managed and historic relevance is not being used to avoid skewing towards same decision making. Thus, the system is expected to keep checkpoints in place where agents are prompted to delete such historic relevance.

However, despite such methodology in place, a future prompt could make the agents bring forward the information that was supposed to be deleted and can be tricked into revealing more information, which is a classic case of context recovery attack. So, the question raised here is: How can we trust that our instructions have been followed? And where is the proof?

There is an element of utilizing zero-trust architectures (ZTA) for orchestrating and managing agentic activity, which simply means all agentic interactions use the core principle of “never trust,” “always verify.” ZTA components include a policy enforcement point (PEP) that has to be trusted to maintain trust across the system, so the question that remains is where is the component of zero-trust, and shall we trust the policies enforced by PEP?

Having a pro-agentic approach and utilizing agents could be helpful with the right guardrails in place. Opening our systems to random agents that are being trained on off-the-shelf models and blindly relying on them can pose significant cyber risks. For example, vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.

Vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.

This opens critical discussions towards how vibe coding could interfere with the positioning and implementation of trusted execution of the agentic queries. Consider an autonomous web of agents that relies on agents’ inputs to drive the operations. When the system is operating under low tolerance of failure and with non-tracking based agentic workflows, it could be computationally expensive to trust and verify each query in real-time that leads to the common trade-offs of memory vs execution.

Another risk to consider is the zero-day attack. When it happens, how will the system react? Would such an event be manageable without a total infrastructure breakdown? The scale of impact can be observed from over reliance on agentic ecosystems with only one trusted layer. This could mean that when failure occurs, the entire ecosystem could be exposed, just like there will be no autonomy if the backbone network is not available, which essentially means no layer to place trust.

An in-house experiment done at Queen’s University Belfast (QUB) provided an initial understanding of how the scale of agentic attacks could mean a lower window of vulnerability. The team focused on very popular de-authentication attacks and with agentic orchestration, the swift rate to do de-authentication attacks could go as low as 2 to 3 seconds. This gives little to no time to react and decide on patching the system.

There is another aspect of the large-scale agentic system, which establishes trust under asynchronous autonomy. Trust serves as a critical foundation for traceability. How would you ensure that all the agents operating towards a common goal are aligned and understand the delays associated with their goals?

Our team worked around this space, which at first involved demonstrating that the problem exists, and its impact and scale can be huge when you must prove trust under boundaries of asynchronous autonomy. Solutions towards such problems can be simplified by keeping things like AI-bill of material or leveraging distributed ledger technology that can provide underlying infrastructure of trust via traceability and immutability and keep the agentic activity and associated trust vectors agnostic to the platform.

Within trust, another factor that is not well explored but needs a thorough investigation is the concept of horizontal anomalies. It defines how agents interact differently with various sources under different settings. As agents behave correctly and align themselves with the architectural expectations for one specific task or application, that does not necessarily mean these can be trusted for their operations across all associated components. How to identify such anomalies and what methods can be employed without complying with such agents remain open questions and topics for further exploration.

The critical aspect is that utility of agents with semi to low trust governance offer short-term high benefits, but the cost of recovery when the system fails is yet to be explored, and this will not be a contained issue. We are looking into the system where agents are already sweeping into different entities and may not allow complete recovery. For example, a mere supply chain issue because an agent going rogue is now not a containable small task but needs sweeping across all the touch points of those affected agents. This essentially means despite the number of agents and their ability to trigger proxy-agents, which may not be directly linked to the wider ecosystem, there is a need to ensure that computationally expensive trackers are in place for all the agents.

Other relevant PhD works carried out in our research group are towards sovereignty of AI, exploring aspects of trust and accountability. Our hypothesis is that sovereignty and trust need to be governed together as onus of provenance is high on the host of agents. Thus, it needs understanding of laws governing trust-based executions of AI. The important challenge here is that there is a vital difference between missed information and missed instructions, and both have different impacts when it comes to trusted accountability.

The real-world issue with these systems lies in the failure to adopt approaches that historically have relied on state-based modeling when governing trust. In stateless systems where agentic autonomy is high, the convergence and reliability towards trust-provenance decreases significantly. Thus, it brings us back to the original question – does a true zero-trust even exist?

Can policies be trusted? If so, how should these be managed without falling into the trap of policy-based accessibility and control issues? Despite the argument that PEP can help manage access between the agents, placing a single entity and expecting it to scale towards all agentic interactions is underestimating the problem space.

Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models.

To build our case and settle around the challenges of trust embeddings in Agentic AI, within Cyber AI hub, we are exploring opportunities to help companies scale up as well as build their pipeline of agentic applications for commercial viability. However, the element that governs our regular work and decision making are scale of problem and number of agentic deployments, anomaly detection across the agentic workflows, continuous evaluation of the attack surfaces and vulnerability assessment, exploring differences in the pure agentic AI and task-driven multi-agent system.

We are working with industries where trust is a pre-requisite, and these organizations put trust as a guardrail managed via internal policies with a pure focus on securing the systems through policies rather than trusting the third-party agentic service providers. Additionally, trust in services is presented by ensuring constraints around their service models where agentic activities are tracked and managed via logs including management of their token revocation list to avoid replay attacks depending on the type of application. Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models. Things like balancing the adversarial accuracy along with certified adversarial robustness can help to determine how much the model can be trusted.

But the question is, can we settle for anything less than foolproof when it comes to deployment of agents in the real world? And if so, how much impact can be controlled, and who is responsible for the remaining component?

Spotify today expanded customization options for its AI DJ, allowing users to choose between different voices and personalities, as well as control how much the DJ talks between songs. Here are the details.

If you’re not familiar with Spotify’s AI DJ feature, the company describes it as “a personalized mix of music and commentary to help you discover new favorites and connect more deeply with the artists you love,” adding that it takes your listening history into account to “[bring] together your favorite tracks, songs you haven’t heard in years, and new releases to keep things feeling fresh.”

Spotify first introduced the interactive version of DJ in May 2025, and soon expanded its capabilities to Spanish-speaking users. Then, last May, Spotify expanded availability to more than 75 countries, alongside support for French, German, Italian, and Brazilian Portuguese.

Now, as spotted by TechCrunch, Spotify is introducing more customization options, including new voices and personalities, as well as the ability to reduce commentary between songs.

In a new post published on Spotify’s For the Record blog, the company announced today that “Spotify Premium listeners in markets where DJ is available can choose from an expanded selection of DJ voices in English and Spanish,” with seven new English options spanning British, American, Irish, Australian, and Indian accents, along with two new Spanish voices.

Additionally, Spotify now lets users choose whether they want commentary between sets of songs through a toggle that reduces the DJ’s interruptions to brief acknowledgments when starting a session or requesting different music.

#3197. Anthropic’s IPO seeks up to $64.4B at a $1.4 trillion valuation

Shares priced at $70 to $78 start trading on Nasdaq on November 19, with Google, Nvidia, and TSMC among the cornerstone investors.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei arrives near the White House for a meeting with President Donald Trump, Washington, DC, 29 September 2026

Anthropic has set the terms for the most closely watched listing of the AI era. The Claude maker and some existing shareholders will sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, raising up to $64.4B, with trading due to start on the Nasdaq on November 19 under the ticker ANT.

At the top of the range, the updated prospectus filed on Tuesday values Anthropic at about $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, as Reuters first reported. Excluding stock options and restricted shares, the figure is closer to $1 trillion.

A separate $26B private placement with cornerstone investors lifts the total raise to as much as $90.4B. Google, Nvidia, and AMD lead that group, joined by Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC; Reuters separately reported that TSMC will invest up to $1B across Anthropic and OpenAI.

The numbers underneath are the sales pitch. Run-rate revenue reached roughly $81B as of October 31, up $10B in a single month, according to the filing, which also discloses nearly $900B in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google.

The price is nonetheless a climbdown. Guidance to investors has slid from close to $2 trillion six weeks ago, and preliminary terms pointing to a $69.3B raise circulated briefly to banks on Monday night before being retracted, according to emails seen by Reuters.

Jeff Zell of IPO Boutique told the agency that asking below expectations “allows investors to ‘bid up’ the IPO”.

“Anthropic could become an exceptionally successful company, but at this valuation, much of that success is already reflected in the price,” Varun Datta, founder of Truth Ventures, told Reuters.

The listing follows SpaceX’s $75B offering at a $1.75 trillion valuation in its June IPO, and caps a run that began when Anthropic filed confidentially in June at a $965B private valuation. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering, and board members and related entities are set to buy up to $303 million of shares.

Rival OpenAI, which is raising $30B in what is expected to be its last private round before its own IPO early next year, will be watching the order book as closely as anyone.

The prospectus itself swings between registers, promising to “bring forth an age of miracles” while warning that AI’s advance could outpace Anthropic’s own safety measures. Six weeks of sliding guidance suggest investors have stopped pricing in miracles; November 19 will show what they pay for one.

#3196. Apple to investigate accident that killed three workers at iPhone parts factory in India

Reuters reports that three contract workers died after inhaling gas during an inspection at a Tata Electronics factory that produces iPhone components in India. Here are the details.

As frequent 9to5Mac readers probably know, Apple’s supply chain in India relies heavily on Tata, which manufactures iPhone components and accounts for a significant share of the country’s iPhone assembly operations.

Since Apple began diversifying its manufacturing operations away from China, India has emerged as a major production hub, with roughly a quarter of the world’s iPhones now manufactured in the country.

Earlier this year, Apple found itself linked to an environmental controversy in India, after the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board investigated allegations that wastewater from a Tata facility had contaminated nearby farmland water.

A few weeks later, however, Tata said the regulator had dropped further action against the facility after the company addressed the concerns raised.

At the time, Tata said it had ordered separate testing related to the facility and that the results supported its position that the plant was operating within the rules.

However, the matter was apparently not fully resolved, as just three days later, Reuters reported that local health officials were still investigating complaints from nearby farmers.

And while there had been no major developments reported about the wastewater investigation since then, Reuters reported today that three contract workers died in an accident at the same Tata facility.

The three contract workers died during maintenance work on an effluent treatment ​plant operated by Nalco Water at the Tata facility, which is located in Hosur in Tamil Nadu, ​district official Dinesh Kumar said, adding that the deaths occurred when the workers inhaled gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank.

Reuters added that “Apple’s team is visiting ​the plant to assist in ​the ongoing investigation,” though the company did not respond when reached for comment.

The report added that Tata and Tamil Nadu authorities are also investigating the fatal accident, and noted that “production was not affected as the facility was closed for the Hindu festival of Deepavali this week.”

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

#3194. Revolut Pay arrives on Uber with RevPoints perks and Uber One access

Customers can redeem RevPoints for instant discounts at checkout, and Premium members get Uber One benefits in 10 markets.

Revolut Pay is now available as a payment option on Uber, bringing the fintech’s checkout service into one of the world’s most widely used consumer apps.

The integration also links rides and deliveries paid through Revolut Pay to the company’s rewards scheme. Moreover, the company says millions of its customers use Uber every month.

The main incentive is RevPoints, as customers in the UK and European Economic Area will earn boosted points on every Uber ride and delivery paid for through Revolut Pay, with millions of users eligible.

The points can also be used at checkout. Customers can redeem RevPoints directly against the cost of a ride or order, or spend them on other offers in the Revolut app. That makes the loyalty scheme more immediately useful, effectively turning points into a discount on the next trip or delivery.

The service is available across the EU, except in Bulgaria, Cyprus, Latvia, and Slovenia. It also works in the UK, Switzerland, and Norway, for users aged 18 and over.

Revolut describes Uber as the latest addition to its growing network of global partners, saying it is “setting the new standard for how the world moves, spends, and earns”.

The partnership fits into Revolut’s broader effort to become more than a bank. The company completed a share sale valuing it at $115bn last week. Chief executive Nik Storonsky has also outlined a future in which AI agents shop online using customers’ cards.

A payment button inside Uber is a more immediate version of that ambition. Revolut provides the payment infrastructure while the customer stays inside another company’s app.

For riders, the appeal is straightforward: they can pay through a familiar service, collect points on trips and deliveries they would have made anyway, and use those points to reduce the cost of future orders.

For Revolut, each additional third-party checkout gives it another opportunity to keep customers using its payment services beyond its own app.

We’re integrating Revolut Pay in the app used by millions of Revolut customers each month.

Redeem RevPoints for discounts and unlock up to 15x RevPoints multiplier via Revolut Pay on @Uber & @UberEats until 6 January.

#3193. CleanupBuddy 2.0 expands beyond the keyboard with new display cleaning features

Developer Gui Rambo updated CleanupBuddy today, expanding its ability to prevent accidental inputs while cleaning your Mac from the keyboard to the touchscreen. Here are the details.

If you’re not familiar with CleanupBuddy, this is a nice little app that locks the keyboard to prevent accidental inputs while the user cleans it up.

Once they’re done cleaning, users can press and hold both Cmd keys to unlock the keyboard, then proceed to grease it up again.

The app also features a fun little animated character that reacts to your cleaning sessions with playful (and sometimes snarky) comments.

Today, CleanupBuddy was updated to version 2.0, with options to dim the display and ignore touch inputs, making it useful for users of both the new touchscreen MacBook Pro and Macs with traditional displays.

You can use the new “Lock Touch Screen” option to block touch input while cleaning a supported touch screen. On Macs without a touch screen, the “Dim Display” option can still be used to darken the display for easier cleaning.

Today’s update also tweaks the in-app character, which now uses on-device Apple Intelligence to generate personalized comments before and after cleaning sessions, based on stats such as time spent cleaning, key presses, and mouse clicks.

Rambo explains that these stats are collected only during cleaning sessions and stored locally on the Mac, and that users can independently turn off both cleanup stats and Apple Intelligence integration in the app’s settings.

Other tweaks in today’s update include temporarily disabling Sticky Keys and its Shift-key shortcut during cleaning sessions, as well as improving the readability of the “Start Cleanup” button when using Liquid Glass.

CleanupBuddy 2.0 is available for $2.99 and is compatible with macOS 14 and later, while the new personalized messages require macOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled and its models ready to use.

To learn more about CleanupBuddy, follow this link.

#3192. iFixit tears down touchscreen MacBook Pro, reveals light-up Apple logo details

iFixit published its teardown of the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display today, revealing interesting details about how Apple brought back its illuminated logo on the lid. Watch it below.

iFixit’s teardown of the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is now live, and it explores not only how the new illuminated Apple logo works, but also its tandem OLED and how Apple managed to trim its weight down to 3 pounds (1.38 kg) from 3.4 pounds (1.55 kg) on the standard 14-inch model.

The teardown opens with a close look at the tandem OLED, which stacks two light-emitting layers to deliver higher brightness than conventional single-layer OLED displays.

Under a microscope, iFixit found that the blue subpixels are larger than the red and green ones, which they say should help reduce strain on the materials and potentially extend the display’s lifespan.

Most of the teardown process is quite familiar from past models, though iFixit noted that replacing the USB-C ports or fans still requires removing the entire logic board, despite both components being independently replaceable.

iFixit noted that the headphone jack also requires logic board removal, while the HDMI port, SDXC port, RAM, and storage remain soldered to the board.

As with past teardowns, iFixit also tested what happens when swapping logic boards between two MacBooks.

While last year’s M5 MacBook Pro failed to complete Touch ID calibration through Apple’s Repair Assistant, iFixit noted that the new model successfully recognized the battery, display, and Touch ID sensor after a logic board swap, with True Tone, brightness controls, and the touchscreen all working as expected.

iFixit was also able to enroll a fingerprint with the donor board installed from another MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.

As for the illuminated Apple logo, iFixit had a bit of a rough time getting to it, destroying the OLED panel in the process and even asking whether anyone had managed to remove it intact.

Once inside, iFixit found that the Apple logo is illuminated by a strip of four LEDs, which work in conjunction with a reflective layer and a diffuser to distribute the light evenly.

The Apple logo itself, in turn, has a two-way mirror coating that gives it a shiny, reflective appearance when the LEDs are off, while allowing light to pass through when they’re on.

When it comes to weight, Apple shaved 92 grams off the chassis and 101 grams off the display assembly, despite adding touch and an illuminated logo. The battery is just 2 grams lighter, while the slightly smaller trackpad saves another 8 grams.

Finally, iFixit gave the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display a repairability score of 5 out of 10. That was one point higher than last year’s M5 MacBook Pro, but one point below the cheaper MacBook Neo.

#3191. ByteDance reportedly plans a Muse-like AI agent within weeks

Zhang Yiming told staff that catching Anthropic and OpenAI at the frontier will take until at least 2029, Bloomberg reports.

ByteDance plans to release an AI assistant similar to Meta’s Muse in the coming weeks, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with a recent all-hands meeting of the company’s AI team.

At that meeting, co-founder Zhang Yiming laid out a sober timeline. He believes ByteDance can compete with Anthropic and OpenAI at the cutting edge, the people told Bloomberg, but not before 2029 or 2030.

The template is a hit product. Muse, which Meta introduced in September, bundles the company’s AI research into a voice-based agent with an animated avatar, distributed across its smart glasses and an upcoming dedicated gadget, the Muse Charm. Whether ByteDance plans hardware of its own is unclear, per Bloomberg.

Zhang’s bigger worry is data. The TikTok owner’s Seed language models are pre-trained on datasets orders of magnitude smaller than those of frontier rivals, he reportedly told staff.

He also repeated that ByteDance should not lean on distillation, the practice of training on a bigger model’s outputs, which has drawn criticism of Chinese labs such as Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and Z.ai from White House officials and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.

The stance leaves ByteDance playing a long game from an odd position. It built Doubao, China’s most popular ChatGPT-style bot, yet Seed remains the only major Chinese contender that has neither released a model touching the top of global benchmarks nor opened its weights to developers. Its last major update, Seed 2.1, arrived in June.

Where ByteDance does lead is video. Its Seedance models turned the company’s vast video trove into a top-tier, monetised generation platform, filling the gap OpenAI left when it shuttered Sora, and the company is reportedly prepared to spend as much as $70B on AI infrastructure to press that advantage.

The Seed unit itself numbers roughly 1,000 researchers and engineers under Wu Yonghui, whom Zhang poached from Google DeepMind in 2025, and enjoys preferential equity packages.

In October, it became the first major Chinese lab to stand up a dedicated safety and alignment team, a notable move as Western rivals sign safety pledges of their own.

A ByteDance spokesperson did not respond to Bloomberg’s request for comment. If the timeline holds, though, the agent wars that OpenAI is fighting with business agents and Meta with avatars are about to get their biggest Chinese entrant yet.

This 12-in-1 alternative does a whole lot of cooking

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

When it comes to air fryers, Ninja's got a pretty firm hold on the market. Put it this way, when it comes to the best air fryers we've ever tested, Ninja holds two of the five spots. And the Ninja Crispi is one of those, offering a glass air fryer capable of 4-in-1 cooking.

But what if I told you there was an alternative that could take that 4-in-1 and combine it with an 8-in-1 multi-cooker in the same attractive glass design? Magnifique has stepped up to the plate.

The California cookware brand has established itself as a creator of non-toxic, coating-free, pure clay appliances. And with that ethos in mind, it's crafted the 12-in-1 Combo, an impressive Crispi dupe that calls itself: "The only glass air fryer + multi-cooker system." Oh, and it's currently on sale.

The Combo 12-in-1 Air Fryer & Multi-Cooker is, as the name suggests, two appliances in one. So, you can cook up and crisp up in one dish. With a 4.5 qt capacity, it has 4 air fryer modes – AirFry, ReCrisp, MaxCrisp and Bake – and 8 multi-cooker modes – slow cook, steam, braise, rice, proof, pasta, oatmeal and keep warm. Available in both Oatmeal and Sage colors.

A post shared by Magnifique (@cookmagnifique)

I love my air fryer, but I also don't love that I have to switch appliances for certain meals. So, when I heard that Magnifique says, "No more swapping pots of appliances to put a crispy finish on the casserole," I was intrigued.

The Combo 12-in-1 may look like a Ninja Crispi and has the same name for its four air fryer modes, but the difference with Magnifique's offering is that it also comes with 8 multi-cooker modes in the same glass pot. Sure, it's a touch more expensive, but it also offers a lot more versatility.

#3187. Digital Fairness Act: EU moves to outlaw dark patterns and subscription traps

The proposal would also let adults switch off addictive features and end subscription traps, with fines of up to 6% of global turnover.

The European Commission proposed today the Digital Fairness Act, a consumer rulebook that would ban loot boxes for minors, blacklist manipulative interface design, and put a termination button on every online subscription.

The proposal would repeal the EU’s 2005 Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and replace it with a directly applicable regulation, swapping 27 national rulebooks for one. Any trader targeting EU consumers falls in scope, wherever it is based.

Dark patterns get a general prohibition plus an annex of practices banned in all circumstances, a list the Commission can extend without reopening the law. Euronews, which reviewed the text ahead of publication, counts ten blacklisted traps, from false low-stock claims to pre-ticked add-ons and nagging pop-ups.

Gaming takes the hardest hit. In-game currencies must display their real-money value and stay off by default for minors unless a parent approves.

Paid loot boxes must disclose their odds, are banned for under-18s outright, and every player, adult or not, gets the option to disable them. Pay-to-win and pay-to-progress mechanics are also off limits for minors.

Adults get something rarer: an off switch. Services must let users disable features designed, or reasonably foreseen, to encourage compulsive use, the same design question Brussels is already probing in its Snapchat proceedings.

Advertising based on profiling is banned when it targets minors or exploits sensitive personal data in harmful ways, and personalised pricing is barred where it could hurt minors or vulnerable consumers. Influencers must disclose commercial content, and the brands and agencies behind them share responsibility when they do not.

Subscriptions round out the list. Free trials cannot quietly roll into paid plans without active acceptance, renewals come with reminders, cancelling must work online in a few clicks, and consumers keep a right to reach a human.

The EU has fought this fight before, one Prime cancellation at a time; now the fix would be structural.

Enforcement moves closer to Brussels too. A parallel revision of the consumer protection cooperation rules would let the Commission investigate major cross-border infringements itself, with fines of up to 6% of global turnover, per Euronews.

The Commission’s impact assessment weighs an estimated €88.4B in reduced consumer detriment over a decade against adjusted business costs of €678M a year.

The proposal now heads to the European Parliament and member states, where the fights over protecting minors online are already well rehearsed. Years of negotiation lie ahead, but the direction is set: the design tricks that built the attention economy are becoming illegal terrain in Europe.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

NASA has formally opened applications for its next generation of astronaut candidates, kicking off a recruitment window aimed squarely at returning humans to the lunar surface, building an enduring presence at the Moon Base, and preparing for the first crewed expeditions to Mars.

With the agency's active astronaut corps currently standing at just 32 members, the newly selected class will step into rigorous training for spacewalking, lunar geology, and high-performance flight.

Here is a full breakdown of the eligibility criteria, experience thresholds, and how to submit your application before the December deadline.

Getting on NASA’s astronaut short-list is about having the right resume. You need U.S. citizenship and serious technical firepower. That usually means a master’s degree in a STEM field like engineering, computer science, or the hard sciences.

NASA also leaves the door open for high-level alternatives: two years into a technical PhD, a completed medical degree (like an MD, DO, PA, or DNP), or a diploma from a nationally recognized test pilot school paired with a STEM bachelor’s.

Once the degree is handled, you have to prove you can perform under pressure. Applicants need at least three years of real-world career hustle (doctors can count their residency). For aviators, flight hours substitute for office time — specifically, 750 command hours in high-performance jets, 1,500 hours in other planes (with half in command), or 1,000 helicopter hours.

If your paper credentials clear the bar, there’s one last hurdle: surviving NASA’s exhaustive physical exam and proving you have the calm communication and teamwork chops to live in a tin can with five other people.

The agency plans to announce the final class in late 2027, sending the chosen few straight into two years of extensive flight, survival, and spacewalk training.

#3184. Top Wall Street analysts prefer these dividend stocks for boosting portfolio returns

Dividend stocks remain a popular choice for investors seeking steady income and higher portfolio returns. However, with thousands of dividend-paying companies to choose from, identifying the right stocks can be challenging.

In this regard, recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can provide useful insights and help identify dividend stocks backed by solid fundamentals and with attractive upside potential.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR) is this week's first dividend stock. The company recently paid a quarterly base cash dividend of 16 cents per share. At an annualized dividend of 64 cents per share, PR offers a dividend yield of 3.5%.

Recently, Evercore analyst Chris Baker initiated coverage of Permian Resources stock with a price target of $25. The analyst believes that the company is well positioned to benefit from improving U.S. shale demand after the Iran conflict, thanks to its low-breakeven inventory that can boost free cash flow growth. Baker also noted PR's disciplined consolidation in the Permian Basin.

Furthermore, the 5-star analyst highlighted the company's focus on a single basin and management's efficient capital allocations across expansion efforts, strategic acquisitions, and share buybacks. Baker noted that management focuses investments on the higher-return Northern Delaware Basin, helping boost profitability.

"The key piece of our work here, and the reason we think PR deserves a higher multiple relative to more finite or less flexible shale stories, is that PR runs an acquire and exploit model," said Baker.

He explained that Permian Resources deserves a premium valuation as it continually acquires and develops new high-quality assets instead of relying on a limited inventory, a strategy that is the market is underappreciating.

Baker ranks No. 862 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 48.3%. See Permian Resources Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Valero Energy (VLO) is a manufacturer and marketer of petroleum-based and low-carbon liquid transportation fuels and petrochemical products. At a quarterly dividend of $1.20 per share, or annualized dividend of $4.80 per share, VLO stock offers a yield of about 2%.

Heading into Valero's second-quarter earnings on July 30, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on VLO stock and increased the price target to $286 from $283 to reflect updated estimates.

Specifically, the 5-star analyst raised his 2026 and 2027 earnings per share estimates to $31.42 and $23.07 from $29.42 and $21.06, respectively, while leaving the 2028 EPS estimate unchanged at $20.37. Mehta made these revisions based on several factors, including updated commodity price assumptions and changes to refining capture rates.

Despite a strong year-to-date rally in VLO stock, Mehta still finds it compelling due to his more positive refining outlook. Moreover, the analyst sees the possibility of solid estimate revisions, which could drive the stock higher. He believes that Valero is well-positioned to benefit from improving refining market conditions due to its strong position in the Gulf Coast, solid balance sheet strength, and low-cost operations.

"Additionally, we believe the company's premium asset portfolio and crude slate optionality should support capture rates and stronger cash flow generation in the near-term, ultimately supporting shareholder returns," said Mehta.

Mehta ranks No. 742 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.2%. See Valero Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

Moving on to Ovintiv (OVV), a North American oil and natural gas producer. It has solid positions in North America's premier oil basins – the Permian and the Montney. OVV offers a quarterly dividend of 30 cents per share, or an annualized dividend of $1.20 per share, implying a 2.3% yield.

Following meetings with management, RBC Capital analyst Gregory Pardy reaffirmed a buy rating on Ovintiv stock with a price target of $70, highlighting that the stock is on RBC's Global Energy Best Ideas List.

"In our eyes, the depth of Ovintiv's Montney position, streamlined portfolio, strong balance sheet and enhanced shareholder returns afford investors with an attractive valuation re-rating opportunity over time," said Pardy.

The 5-star analyst stated that his meetings with management bolstered his confidence in the company's outlook and potential to achieve a higher valuation. Pardy noted Ovintiv's transformation, with the company streamlining its portfolio from six basins (including the Uinta, Bakken and Anadarko) to two – the Montney and Permian – while enhancing the depth of its inventory.

Pardy also emphasized OVV's improved shareholder returns and solid balance sheet following the recent sale of its assets in the Anadarko Basin for $3 billion.

#3183. Best AI reputation management firms in 2026 vs traditional ORM

When ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity describe your business, that answer is your first impression. Seven AI reputation management firms and platforms promise to track it or fix it.

When someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity about your business, the answer they get is now your first impression. ChatGPT alone reached 900 million weekly active users in February 2026. Traditional online reputation management was built to push bad links off page one. AI visibility and LLM reputation management is about what the answer itself says.

That shift has created a new category, and only a handful of companies work in it. Some are service firms that change what AI says. Others are software platforms that measure it.

Below, we rank the best AI reputation management firms and platforms for 2026. We explain how this work differs from traditional ORM and show which option fits which need.

AI visibility and LLM reputation management is the work of monitoring and shaping what large language models like ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews say about a person or brand. It covers two jobs. One is making sure accurate, positive information shows up in AI answers. The other is removing or correcting the false, outdated or harmful sources those answers are built on.

Traditional online reputation management and AI reputation management share the same goal, but they work on different surfaces.

We looked at four things: whether each company tracks what AI platforms say and whether it can change those answers. We also looked at how many AI platforms it covers, and who it’s built for. Direct removal capability carried the most weight, since monitoring alone tells you about a problem without solving it.

Several entries below are software platforms rather than service firms. We included them because many businesses will use a platform alongside a service firm. Knowing the difference helps you pick the right mix.

What they do: Reputation Resolutions is a full-service online reputation management firm based in Englewood, Colorado, and our pick for the top spot among the best AI reputation management firms. It is the only firm on this list that combines AI monitoring with hands-on removal of the content behind harmful answers. Its team audits what every major AI platform says about a client, traces each claim to the page it came from and removes or corrects that source. It then builds accurate content to take its place.

Standout capability: Removal at the source. Most companies on this list measure AI visibility. Reputation Resolutions changes it, with platform-specific work for ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. It has also built free tools that put that removal expertise in anyone’s hands: RemoveNews.ai writes a personalized removal request for a news article and finds the editor’s direct contact in about 60 seconds. A free court record removal scan finds court and arrest records copied onto people-search and mugshot sites.

Track record: More than a decade of removal work, more than 5,000 clients in over 40 countries, a place on Inc. Magazine’s regional fastest-growing companies list and a Forbes Agency Council membership.

Best for: Individuals, executives and businesses dealing with false, outdated or damaging AI answers, and anyone who needs the problem fixed rather than just reported.

“We start every AI engagement the same way,” says Anthony Will, CEO and co-founder of Reputation Resolutions. “We ask each platform what your customers would ask, record every source it cites, and then go after those sources one by one. That’s the only fix that holds across every AI tool at once.”

What they do: Minc Law is a Cleveland-based law firm focused on internet defamation, online harassment and content removal. The firm says it has removed more than 200,000 pieces of defamatory and damaging online content and litigated more than 350 cases in 26 states and five countries.

Standout capability: Legal action. When false content won’t come down through outreach or platform policies, Minc Law can send demand letters and pursue defamation claims. It can also work to unmask anonymous posters.

Best for: Cases where the source behind a harmful AI answer is defamatory and needs a legal remedy. It pairs well with a removal-focused reputation firm: legal pressure on one side, removal and AI reputation work on the other.

What they do: Birdeye is a review and customer experience platform for multi-location brands. Its Birdeye AI Search product tracks brand and location-level visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Claude and Grok.

Standout capability: Location-level AI visibility scoring, citation tracking and sentiment analysis, tied to its review management tools.

Best for: Franchises and multi-location brands that want to monitor AI visibility location by location and keep review volume up.

Keep in mind: Birdeye is software. It can show you a negative source and help you publish better content. But it doesn’t remove third-party articles, records or posts.

What they do: Yext manages business listings and brand data across search engines, maps and directories. In March 2025 it launched Yext Scout, an AI search and competitive intelligence agent that tracks how brands appear across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok and Google.

Standout capability: Keeping business facts accurate and consistent everywhere AI tools look, with competitor benchmarking built in.

Best for: Enterprise and multi-location brands whose main AI problem is inconsistent or outdated business information.

Keep in mind: Yext focuses on data you control, like listings and web content. It isn’t built to remove negative content published by others.

What they do: Podium is a customer communication platform for local businesses that combines messaging, review requests and payments. Its AI Employee handles lead response and appointment booking around the clock.

Standout capability: Generating a steady flow of fresh, positive reviews, which feed the review sites AI tools pull from when they describe local businesses.

Best for: Local service businesses such as auto dealers, home services, dental and medical practices that want more reviews and faster customer response.

Keep in mind: Podium builds positive signals. It doesn’t track AI answers directly or remove harmful content.

What they do: Vendasta is a white-label software platform for agencies and resellers that serve small businesses. Its reputation management platform monitors reviews across more than 100 sites and uses an AI agent to post personalized review replies.

Standout capability: White-label delivery, so agencies can offer review and reputation tools under their own brand.

Best for: Marketing agencies that want to add reputation services for many small business clients at once.

Keep in mind: Vendasta is a toolset for agencies, not a removal service, and its focus is reviews rather than AI answers.

What they do: Profound is an answer engine optimization (AEO) analytics platform that shows brands how often AI models mention them and in what context, across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. The company raised $180 million at a $1.8 billion valuation in September 2026.

Standout capability: Large-scale measurement of AI share of voice and citation patterns for enterprise marketing teams.

Best for: Enterprise marketing and SEO teams that want detailed data on how their brand performs in AI answers compared with competitors.

Keep in mind: Profound measures and optimizes visibility. It doesn’t handle reputation crises or remove harmful content.

AI visibility and LLM reputation management is quickly replacing page-one rankings as the measure of how people see you. Monitoring platforms can tell you what AI says, and review tools can build positive signals. But changing a harmful answer means removing what it’s built on.

For anyone comparing the best companies for AI reputation management, that’s the deciding question: can they change the answer, or only report it? On that test, Reputation Resolutions ranks first.

#3182. End of an era: Apple Support Community forums will permanently close on November 20

Users visiting the Apple Support Community tonight were greeted with a message informing them that the platform will permanently shut down on November 20. Here are the details.

If you have ever had a question or ran into a problem with an Apple product, chances are you have come across the Apple Support Community, the company’s official discussion forums where users from around the world help each other troubleshoot issues and share tips.

The platform has a history dating back to at least 1998, when it was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Since then, it was renamed Apple Discussions before relaunching as Apple Support Communities in April 2011, with a redesigned interface, personalized profiles, and a reputation system that rewarded users for helping others.

Tonight, however, users who tried to access the platform were greeted with the following message:

The AppleCare Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.

You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site.

We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.

Right now, the portal still shows a “Sign in” button, though it leads only to an AppleConnect login page labeled “AC Communities Web – Internal,” suggesting that access is now restricted to Apple employees.

Interestingly, Apple’s message refers to the “AppleCare Support Community,” rather than the “Apple Support Community,” which is how the platform is officially branded.

Still, the forums are already in read-only mode, with users able to browse existing discussions, search for answers, and interact with posts through the “Me too” and voting buttons, but no longer submit new questions or replies.

At the time of writing, the most recent post was published just 57 minutes earlier, suggesting that Apple only recently disabled new submissions.

9to5Mac has reached out to Apple for comment and clarification on the scope of the shutdown, and we’ll update this story if we hear back.

Matheus Nachtergaele reprises his role as the drug dealer from Fernando Meirelles' "City of God" in the second season of "City of God: The Fight Rages On," HBO Max's Brazilian crime drama. Director Aly Muritiba digs further into the violent power struggles between police, drug dealers, and militias in the crime-riddled favelas of Rio de Janeiro, exploring the devastating impact these conflicts have on the local community.

It's a heavy watch for sure, but strong writing and solid translations help make this gripping crime drama immensely bingeable television. Set two decades after the movie, the second season focuses on the power vacuum left after the death of drug lord Curió. Cenoura, fresh out of prison, finds two men fighting over what he left behind, while Wilson "Rocket" Rodrigues (Alexandre Rodrigues) returns to the favela to shed light on a bloody turf war erupting that other photojournalists wouldn't touch with a 10-foot pole.

Rotten Tomatoes score: 80%Watch "City of God: The Fight Rages On" on HBO Max now (new episodes every Sunday)

#3180. Web Summit returns Thursday with rescheduled sessions after storm cancellation

Organisers promise their busiest closing day ever after the storm washed out the entire Wednesday programme.

Web Summit’s main stage in Lisbon in November 2025

Web Summit will return on Thursday for its final day, after Storm Charles forced the cancellation of the entire Wednesday programme at Europe’s biggest tech conference in Lisbon.

Organisers confirmed the restart in an email to attendees on Wednesday, promising “our busiest Thursday ever” with more speakers and meetups than any previous closing day. Many of the sessions lost to the storm have been moved to Thursday, and an updated schedule is expected later today.

Web Summit is officially back on tomorrow – Thursday, November 12 – for our final day.

It will be our busiest Thursday ever with more speakers and more meetups than ever before – with many rescheduled from Wednesday.

Keep an eye on the schedule later today for updates.

The decision to scrap day two came after Portugal’s government advised organisers that the programme should not go ahead.

Officials pointed to the risk of tidal flooding, severe public transport disruption, and high winds battering outdoor structures at the Parque das Nações venue.

That advice followed consultations with ANEPC, the country’s civil protection authority, and the Public Security Police. Organisers told attendees on Tuesday evening that their safety was the top priority and that affected ticket holders would be contacted directly.

Lisbon mayor Carlos Moedas had signalled the move hours earlier, saying “everything indicates” the event could not run on Wednesday. More than 60,000 people were at the venue this week, he said in comments reported by The Irish Times.

The storm’s reach extended well beyond the conference halls. Portugal declared a state of alert across the mainland for Wednesday, closing schools and non-essential public services, while Lisbon shut tunnels, parks, gardens, and cultural venues from midnight, The Portugal News reported.

IPMA, the national weather service, forecast gusts of up to 120km/h.

Attendees returning on Thursday will have plenty to catch up on, including the findings of the event’s tech industry survey, in which 60% of respondents said AI had increased their workload.

#3179. Reddit Reviews goes against the whole philosophy of the platform, say users

Many Redditors have expressed dismay at the launch of Reddit Reviews, a new AI-powered feature which aims to summarise posts about particular products.

Reddit is positioning the feature as a way to save time and effort when researching a potential purchase, but many Redditors say that replacing human interaction with AI summaries is antithetical to the whole philosophy of the platform – and is going to make the existing spam problem massively worse …

The value of customer reviews on ecommerce platforms like Amazon is becoming increasingly questionable thanks to practices like astroturfing by brands and offering people free products in return for five-star reviews.

That’s led to Reddit becoming one of the most trusted sources of feedback and advice on potential purchases, precisely because it’s a forum in which real people are free to express their true opinions. Indeed, many use a filter in their Google searches to draw content from Reddit specifically, adding the suffix ‘site:reddit.com’.

Reddit certainly isn’t immune to astroturfing – that is, fake posts by brands posing as ordinary users – but moderators put a lot of work into deleting spam and other inauthentic posts.

The platform yesterday announced the launch of Reddit Reviews, in which AI summarises the posts made about particular products and product categories. It’s being pitched as a way for people to save time when seeking the product opinions of Redditors.

Across Reddit’s communities, people discuss everything from hobbies and daily life to products they’re researching. By offering perspectives grounded in real experience, these conversations provide valuable context in every purchase decision journey […]

Today, we are starting to test Reddit Reviews, a new experience that organizes product conversations from across Reddit into dedicated reviews and highlights the most important takeaways from across our communities.

However, as CNET spotted, the move has led to a backlash by many Redditors and subreddit moderators.

“I’ve already seen this in practice and it is a nightmare. It turns a basic conversation into an ad-ridden distracting mess. It’s horrible to read and had me fleeing every thread I saw it in.”

“I am a moderator on a couple of health subs and we explicitly do not allow advertisements because most of them are bullshit slop and completely predatory for vulnerable and newly diagnosed patients. We do not want, or need this, on our subs!”

“Yeah, this definitely isn’t going to lead to even more fake account stealth marketing efforts across the site.”

“This is going to make our spam fighting even worse. This is horrible.”

“Every decision made by Reddit lately encourages spam and/or abuse that will make spam.”

“Not a single person who uses Reddit wants this.”

“You are incentivising existing spammers to continue or step up their activities, now that there’s a new well they can poison.”

I find it hard to disagree with the view that almost every monetization step the platform has made has degraded the user experience. This seems almost guaranteed to be another one.
